title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This sheet is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed page, labelled 'n° 413 – A – 21 –', printed upside down. It is almost certainly a page of a Bourbaki 'rédaction', a circulated draft, whose blank reverse Grothendieck used for his handwritten notes. The neighbouring pages are his notes comparing analytic and topological fundamental classes, with the factor 2iπ; the only connection to this page is the paper.

The typed text belongs to a draft on formal varieties and formal groups in the Cartier–Dieudonné style. Setting:
- K is the base ring and V a formal 'noyau' (germ of a formal variety).
- U(V) is the coalgebra of distributions (hyperalgebra) of V. In a formal chart given by a free module M, U(V) has a divided-power basis e_α indexed by multi-indices.
- U_0(V) = K·1 is the degree-0 part.
- Formal maps from V to a module N are defined as Hom(U(V);N), written P̂(V;N), i.e. formal power series. P̂_+(V;N) is the submodule of maps vanishing on U_0(V), i.e. series without constant term.

Proposition 8 characterises which linear maps ψ: U(V) → U(W) are push-forwards φ_* of formal maps φ ∈ P̂_+(V;W). The conditions are:
- ψ(U_0(V)) = U_0(W);
- ψ is a coalgebra morphism: (ψ⊗ψ)∘Γ = Γ∘ψ, with Γ the diagonal (comultiplication).

Proof sketch:
- Necessity comes from Prop. 6.
- Uniqueness comes from Prop. 7.
- For existence, reduce via formal charts to free modules M, N with bases. Write ψ(e_α) = Σ a_{α,β} e'^β (30).
- Preserving U_0 gives a_{0,β} = 0 for |β| ≥ 1 and a_{0,0} ≠ 0 (31).
- Compatibility with the diagonal gives a_{α,β1+β2} = Σ_{α1+α2=α} a_{α1,β1} a_{α2,β2} (32).
- The page breaks off here. The remaining step is that (32) forces the a_{α,β} to be the coefficients of divided-power expansions of a power series φ with no constant term, so ψ = φ_*.

This is the standard equivalence between formal (pointed) maps and morphisms of the corresponding distribution coalgebras. It underlies Dieudonné's hyperalgebras and Cartier's duality for formal groups.
errors: The text says ψ(U_0(V)) = U_0(W) gives only a_{0,0} ≠ 0. But (32) with α = 0 and β1 = β2 = 0 gives a_{0,0} = a_{0,0}², so a_{0,0} = 1 (assuming no zero divisors, or once counit compatibility is imposed). This is a harmless imprecision.

The bases are introduced as (e_ι)_{ι∈I} with a single index, but formula (30) uses multi-indices α, β for the divided-power basis of U(V). This is a notational slip, or relies on conventions fixed earlier in the draft.
The basis (e'_j) is said to be a basis of M' although the modules were called M and N. This is a typographical inconsistency in the typescript.

ideas.what: Formal maps V→N defined as linear maps on the distribution coalgebra U(V), i.e. formal power series as the dual of divided powers.
ideas.modern_name: Coalgebra of distributions / hyperalgebra; Cartier duality between formal schemes and coalgebras
ideas.where_published: Treated in SGA 3 (Demazure–Gabriel) and Demazure–Gabriel 'Groupes algébriques'; not a Grothendieck text as such

ideas.what: Proposition 8: a linear map between distribution coalgebras comes from a pointed formal map iff it preserves degree 0 and is a coalgebra morphism.
ideas.modern_name: Fully faithful embedding of pointed formal varieties into (irreducible) coalgebras
ideas.where_published: Standard in the formal group literature (Dieudonné, Cartier, Demazure–Gabriel, Hazewinkel)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is the reverse side of a typed Bourbaki-style draft (rédaction n° 413) on formal varieties, reused as scrap paper. Its content is a standard, well-documented result of Dieudonné and Cartier, unrelated to Grothendieck's handwritten notes on the neighbouring pages.
transcription_corrections: The page is typed and printed upside down: it is the verso of a typescript (rédaction n° 413, page A-21), not a handwritten Grothendieck note.
'(e_ι)_{ι∈I}' is consistent with the image, but formula (30) uses multi-indices α, β; e'^β denotes divided-power monomials in U(W).
The basis (e'_j)_{j∈J} is of the second free module. The typescript appears to read 'base de M'' (or N), and the transcription follows it, though the intended module is N.
The pencil '15' in the bottom margin is the archive page number.
